14klnub.q: Keeping the safety distance prevents a collision with the vehicle ahead.
14klnub.why: Keeping a safe following distance lets you brake in time and avoid rear-ending (tamponamento) the vehicle ahead.

1kdccnm.q: The driver must assess the safety distance also on the basis of the speed of the vehicle being driven.
1kdccnm.why: The higher your speed, the more ground you cover while reacting and braking, so the distance must be increased.

51vzf5.q: The driver must set the safety distance also according to his own reflexes.
51vzf5.why: Slower reflexes mean a longer reaction time and more distance travelled before braking, so you need a bigger gap.

5ohsoj.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to traffic conditions.
5ohsoj.why: Traffic affects the safe distance: in heavy or unpredictable traffic sudden braking is more likely, so leave more space.

150hiad.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the layout of the road (gradient and curves).
150hiad.why: Gradients and bends change braking distance and visibility, so they affect how much distance you need.

usiy4q.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to weather conditions.
usiy4q.why: Rain, snow, ice or fog reduce grip and visibility and lengthen braking distance, so the gap must be bigger.

14vvwh.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the type of vehicle being driven.
14vvwh.why: Different vehicles have different weight and braking ability, so the distance needed to stop differs.

1krr75u.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the efficiency of the vehicle.
1krr75u.why: A poorly maintained vehicle (brakes, suspension, tyres) brakes worse and needs a longer distance.

10tawb6.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the size of the load.
10tawb6.why: A heavier load increases mass and braking distance, so the safe distance must grow.

1qg0ejy.q: The safety distance to keep from a snowplough in operation is 20 metres.
1qg0ejy.why: You must keep at least 20 metres from a snowplough that is working.

bldo2x.q: The safety distance to keep from a salt-spreading machine in operation is 20 metres.
bldo2x.why: You must keep at least 20 metres from a salt-spreading machine that is working.

y4kyqj.q: The driver must assess the safety distance also with reference to the speed of the vehicle ahead.
y4kyqj.why: The speed and braking of the vehicle ahead affect the space you need to stop without hitting it.

15d9d8y.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the efficiency of the brakes.
15d9d8y.why: Weak brakes lengthen braking distance, so a bigger gap is needed.

1d9klqd.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the condition of the tyres.
1d9klqd.why: Worn or low-grip tyres lengthen braking distance and call for more space.

1cl3z2t.q: On an extra-urban road with one lane per direction, the distance between goods vehicles with a gross mass over 3.5 tonnes, which are subject to an overtaking ban, must be at least 100 metres.
1cl3z2t.why: On single-carriageway extra-urban roads, goods vehicles over 3.5 t under an overtaking ban (divieto di sorpasso) must keep at least 100 metres apart.

xo9o37.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the type of engine fuel.
xo9o37.why: Fuel type (petrol, diesel, LPG) does not change stopping distance, so it plays no part in the safe distance.

ja33fp.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the engine displacement of the vehicle.
ja33fp.why: Engine displacement does not affect stopping distance; speed, reflexes, grip, brakes and load do.

1ibo9fw.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the engine power.
1ibo9fw.why: Engine power does not change braking distance, so it does not determine the safe distance.

vro91b.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the width of the carriageway.
vro91b.why: Carriageway width does not change the space needed to stop, so it is irrelevant.

1eprqkm.q: The driver must set the safety distance also according to the width of the vehicle he is driving.
1eprqkm.why: Vehicle width has no effect on braking distance, so it does not matter for the safe distance.

17zyc9r.q: The driver is obliged to check that the vehicle behind him keeps the safety distance.
17zyc9r.why: Each driver is responsible only for his own distance from the vehicle ahead, not for that of the vehicle behind.

wt6khx.q: The safety distance to keep from a snowplough in operation is 10 metres.
wt6khx.why: The distance to keep from a working snowplough is at least 20 metres, not 10.

1cu8ctd.q: The safety distance to keep from a salt-spreading machine in operation is 15 metres.
1cu8ctd.why: The distance to keep from a working salt-spreader is at least 20 metres, not 15.

gbkhne.q: The distance between road trains, where overtaking-ban signs apply between them, must be at least 10 metres.
gbkhne.why: Between road trains under an overtaking ban the minimum gap is 100 metres on extra-urban roads, not 10.

1pbdtw9.q: On extra-urban roads, the value of the safety distance is always 70 metres.
1pbdtw9.why: The safe distance is never a fixed value; it varies with speed and with road and vehicle conditions.

1xqnxr6.q: The value of the safety distance must be at least equal to that of the braking distance.
1xqnxr6.why: The safe distance must be at least the distance covered during reaction time, not the braking distance.

18cb0m1.q: The value of the safety distance must be at least equal to that of the visibility distance.
18cb0m1.why: The minimum reference is the distance covered during reaction time, not the visibility distance.

x1jaaz.q: The safety distance does not have to be kept at driving speeds below 50 km/h.
x1jaaz.why: The safe distance must always be kept at any speed; there is no speed below which it can be ignored.

h0u0nw.q: The value of the safety distance must be set also according to the gear engaged.
h0u0nw.why: The gear engaged does not change stopping distance, so it has no effect on the safe distance.

li9yho.q: The safety distance is also proportioned to the driver's psychophysical condition.
li9yho.why: Tiredness, distraction or impairment lengthen reaction time, so the distance must be increased.

s0tic9.q: The safety distance must be kept so as not to rear-end the vehicle ahead.
s0tic9.why: The purpose of the safe distance is to avoid rear-ending (tamponamento) the vehicle ahead.

1eppavh.q: The safety distance must be determined in relation to the width of the vehicle ahead.
1eppavh.why: The width of the vehicle ahead has no effect on braking distance, so it is irrelevant.

520yw2.q: The safety distance is also proportioned to the number of lanes of the road.
520yw2.why: The number of lanes does not change the space needed to stop, so it has no influence.

18ihlqb.q: The safety distance is also proportioned to the presence of power steering.
18ihlqb.why: Power steering does not affect stopping distance, so it does not affect the safe distance.

16iifr0.q: The safety distance is also proportioned to the type of the following vehicle.
16iifr0.why: What counts is your own vehicle, not the one behind; you answer only for your distance from the vehicle ahead.

1qujd24.q: The safety distance is also proportioned to the speed limit shown on the back of the vehicle ahead.
1qujd24.why: A limit shown on the back of a vehicle does not change braking distance; actual speed and conditions do.

2jhb5y.q: The safety distance is a fixed distance.
2jhb5y.why: The safe distance is not fixed; it must be adjusted constantly to speed and to road and vehicle conditions.

1v9v64w.q: The safety distance must be kept above a certain speed.
1v9v64w.why: The safe distance must always be kept at any speed, not only above a certain threshold.

9juvxm.q: The safety distance is also proportioned to the grip of the tyres.
9juvxm.why: Lower tyre grip lengthens braking distance and requires a bigger gap.

t6kv6s.q: The safety distance depends on the distance covered during the reaction time.
t6kv6s.why: The safe distance is based on the distance covered during reaction time, before braking even starts.

1b0002a.q: The safety distance must be at least 100 metres on steep downhill stretches.
1b0002a.why: There is no fixed 100 metres; on steep descents the distance simply has to be increased.

d38lru.q: The safety distance must be at least 100 metres when it is snowing.
d38lru.why: In snow the distance must be increased, but no fixed value of 100 metres is set.

196fv69.q: The safety distance depends on the efficiency of the parking brake.
196fv69.why: The parking brake is not used for braking while driving, so it does not affect the safe distance.

8acksd.q: The safety distance must be greater if one is driving in the emergency lane.
8acksd.why: The emergency lane does not change the safe distance, and it may be used only in emergencies anyway.

jwi7lv.q: The safety distance must be equal to the braking distance increased by 20 metres.
jwi7lv.why: No such fixed formula exists; the distance depends on speed, reflexes and conditions, and must be at least the reaction-time distance.

1qpqjd0.q: The distance covered during the reaction time is that covered from the moment a dangerous situation is perceived to the moment braking begins.
1qpqjd0.why: Reaction-time distance is the distance travelled between perceiving danger and starting to brake.

54qv31.q: The safety distance must be kept to avoid a rear-end collision.
54qv31.why: The safe distance exists to avoid rear-ending (tamponamento) the vehicle ahead.

1wo9b9g.q: The safety distance may be greater than the distance covered during the reaction time.
1wo9b9g.why: The safe distance must be at least the reaction-time distance, but it can and often should be greater.

cxc30l.q: The safety distance must be kept to avoid a head-on collision.
cxc30l.why: The safe distance concerns the vehicle ahead and prevents rear-end collisions, not head-on ones.

fda8a6.q: The safety distance must be kept to avoid a side collision.
fda8a6.why: The safe distance prevents rear-end collisions, not side collisions.

o862hq.q: The safety distance may be less than the distance covered during the reaction time.
o862hq.why: The safe distance cannot be less than the distance covered during reaction time.

1s5zkmh.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 30 km/h is about 9 metres.
1s5zkmh.why: At 30 km/h you cover about 9 metres per second, so the minimum safe distance is about 9 metres.

c8dtlg.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 50 km/h must be about 14 metres.
c8dtlg.why: At 50 km/h you cover about 14 metres per second, so the minimum safe distance is about 14 metres.

o13kcl.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 100 km/h must be about 28 metres.
o13kcl.why: At 100 km/h you cover about 28 metres per second, so the minimum safe distance is about 28 metres.

1yq4ilu.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 150 km/h must be about 42 metres.
1yq4ilu.why: At 150 km/h you cover about 42 metres per second, so the minimum safe distance is about 42 metres.

1d93qm7.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 130 km/h must be about 36 metres.
1d93qm7.why: At 130 km/h you cover about 36 metres per second, so the minimum safe distance is about 36 metres.

15v1nu1.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 30 km/h must be about 2 metres.
15v1nu1.why: At 30 km/h the minimum safe distance is about 9 metres, not 2: roughly the distance covered in one second.

8ox9mu.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 50 km/h must be about 5 metres.
8ox9mu.why: At 50 km/h the minimum safe distance is about 14 metres, not 5: roughly the distance covered in one second.

1srthf1.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 100 km/h must be about 15 metres.
1srthf1.why: At 100 km/h the minimum safe distance is about 28 metres, not 15: roughly the distance covered in one second.

12kj8w4.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 130 km/h must be about 20 metres.
12kj8w4.why: At 130 km/h the minimum safe distance is about 36 metres, not 20: roughly the distance covered in one second.

xw9zx1.q: The minimum safety distance when travelling at 150 km/h must be about 25 metres.
xw9zx1.why: At 150 km/h the minimum safe distance is about 42 metres, not 25: roughly the distance covered in one second.

xh9g53.q: Driver distraction can be a cause of accidents.
xh9g53.why: Distraction at the wheel is one of the most frequent causes of accidents.

8zrm7y.q: Driver distraction can be caused by switching on a mobile phone.
8zrm7y.why: Switching on a phone takes your eyes and attention off the road, and at speed you travel a long way blind.

1h6fls5.q: Driver distraction can be caused by lighting a cigarette.
1h6fls5.why: Lighting a cigarette takes eyes and hands away from driving, creating a moment of danger.

1hkzvez.q: Driver distraction can be caused by searching for the controls of the radio or other electronic devices.
1hkzvez.why: Searching for radio or device controls takes your eyes off the road and causes distraction.

1h4t09s.q: Driver distraction is not caused by the use of the mobile phone.
1h4t09s.why: Using a mobile phone is one of the main causes of distraction while driving.

9snsl5.q: Driver distraction is not a danger if it lasts only a few seconds.
9snsl5.why: Even a few seconds of distraction are dangerous: at speed you travel tens of metres out of control.

n8lokf.q: In one second, you travel about 14 m if driving at 50 km/h.
n8lokf.why: 50 km/h is about 14 metres per second (50 divided by 3.6).

1m1i7e6.q: In one second, you travel about 28 m if driving at 100 km/h.
1m1i7e6.why: 100 km/h is about 28 metres per second (100 divided by 3.6).

13rb8ua.q: In one second, you travel about 36 m if driving at 130 km/h.
13rb8ua.why: 130 km/h is about 36 metres per second (130 divided by 3.6).

1q0ieh.q: In one second, you travel about 42 m if driving at 150 km/h.
1q0ieh.why: 150 km/h is about 42 metres per second (150 divided by 3.6).

fbt2g5.q: In one second, you travel about 20 m if driving at 150 km/h.
fbt2g5.why: At 150 km/h you cover about 42 metres in one second, not 20.

1ys4fpc.q: In one second, you travel about 4 m if driving at 50 km/h.
1ys4fpc.why: At 50 km/h you cover about 14 metres in one second, not 4.

1ge6xc7.q: In one second, you travel about 10 m if driving at 100 km/h.
1ge6xc7.why: At 100 km/h you cover about 28 metres in one second, not 10.

fvxmvb.q: In one second, you travel about 15 m if driving at 130 km/h.
fvxmvb.why: At 130 km/h you cover about 36 metres in one second, not 15.

1pbc0lm.q: The braking distance is the distance travelled from the start of braking until the vehicle stops.
1pbc0lm.why: Braking distance (spazio di frenatura) starts when the brake is applied and ends when the vehicle stops; the reaction time is not included.

142xpsy.q: The braking distance quadruples if the speed doubles.
142xpsy.why: Braking distance grows with the square of the speed: double the speed gives four times the distance.

rmg3r.q: The braking distance becomes nine times greater if the speed triples.
rmg3r.why: Braking distance grows with the square of the speed: triple the speed gives nine times the distance (3 squared).

1vi5ebz.q: The braking distance becomes sixteen times greater if the speed quadruples.
1vi5ebz.why: Braking distance grows with the square of the speed: four times the speed gives sixteen times the distance (4 squared).

1uu8ydh.q: The braking distance is independent of speed.
1uu8ydh.why: Braking distance depends strongly on speed: it increases with the square of the speed.

rh8q47.q: The braking distance doubles if the speed doubles.
rh8q47.why: If speed doubles, braking distance becomes four times greater, not double, because it grows with the square of the speed.

hz8si7.q: The braking distance increases if the grip between tyre and asphalt is low.
hz8si7.why: With low grip the tyres transmit less braking force, so more distance is needed to stop.

4j33cd.q: The braking distance increases if the road is snowy.
4j33cd.why: Snow reduces grip, so the braking distance increases.

1vhoq4z.q: The braking distance increases if the road is wet.
1vhoq4z.why: A wet road reduces grip, so the braking distance increases.

699j2i.q: The braking distance increases if the road slopes downhill.
699j2i.why: Going downhill, gravity pushes the vehicle forward, so the braking distance increases.

1w025ol.q: The braking distance decreases if the road slopes uphill.
1w025ol.why: Going uphill, gravity helps slow the vehicle, so the braking distance decreases.

1ttnscs.q: The braking distance decreases if the driver has quick reflexes.
1ttnscs.why: Reflexes affect the reaction time, i.e. the distance travelled before braking starts, not the braking distance itself.

5oissx.q: The braking distance decreases if the wheels lock.
5oissx.why: Locked wheels lose grip and steering control, so the braking distance increases.

ejsqoj.q: The braking distance decreases on the downhill section of a hump (dosso).
ejsqoj.why: On the downhill side of a hump (dosso), gravity pushes the vehicle forward, so the braking distance increases, not decreases.

24t6m.q: The braking distance increases if the road slopes uphill.
24t6m.why: Going uphill, the braking distance decreases because gravity helps stop the vehicle.

1y7ojun.q: The braking distance decreases if the road slopes downhill.
1y7ojun.why: Going downhill, the braking distance increases because gravity pushes the vehicle forward.

uxlqbq.q: The total stopping distance equals the distance travelled during the reaction time plus the distance travelled during braking.
uxlqbq.why: Total stopping distance (spazio totale di arresto) is the reaction-time distance plus the braking distance.

1t09exw.q: The total stopping distance depends on speed.
1t09exw.why: Speed affects both the reaction-time distance and the braking distance.

1kasazj.q: The total stopping distance depends on tyre wear.
1kasazj.why: Worn tyres grip less and lengthen the braking distance, and therefore the total stopping distance.

1jzjuw4.q: The total stopping distance depends on the condition of the asphalt.
1jzjuw4.why: The road surface determines grip and so the braking distance, which is part of the total stopping distance.

14o377t.q: The total stopping distance is independent of tyre wear.
14o377t.why: Tyre wear reduces grip and lengthens the total stopping distance.

at6gre.q: The total stopping distance is independent of the condition of the asphalt.
at6gre.why: The condition of the asphalt changes grip and therefore the total stopping distance.

q77ir8.q: The total stopping distance equals the distance travelled during the reaction time.
q77ir8.why: Total stopping distance also includes the braking distance, not only the reaction-time distance.

ojw6m5.q: The total stopping distance equals the distance travelled during braking.
ojw6m5.why: Total stopping distance also includes the distance covered during the reaction time, before braking starts.

1wz7re1.q: The total stopping distance does not depend on speed.
1wz7re1.why: Total stopping distance does depend on speed: the faster you go, the longer it is.

1ja2rni.q: The total stopping distance increases if the speed increases.
1ja2rni.why: Higher speed increases both the reaction-time distance and the braking distance.

k9je6u.q: The total stopping distance increases if the road is snowy.
k9je6u.why: Snow reduces grip and lengthens braking, so the total stopping distance increases.

12go30c.q: The total stopping distance increases if the road is covered with mud.
12go30c.why: Mud reduces grip and lengthens braking, so the total stopping distance increases.

1d88mfi.q: The total stopping distance increases if the tyres are worn.
1d88mfi.why: Worn tyres grip less and lengthen braking, so the total stopping distance increases.

1xkaq6j.q: The total stopping distance increases if the tyres are not worn.
1xkaq6j.why: Tyres that are not worn grip well, so they do not increase the stopping distance; it is wear that increases it.

1xbn8tn.q: The total stopping distance increases if the speed decreases.
1xbn8tn.why: If speed decreases, the total stopping distance decreases, not increases.

1wfudms.q: The total stopping distance increases if the asphalt is rough.
1wfudms.why: Rough asphalt gives good grip and does not lengthen the stopping distance; wet, snowy or slippery surfaces do.

91ty8q.q: The driver's concentration affects the safe following distance.
91ty8q.why: If concentration drops, reaction time gets longer, so a greater safe following distance (distanza di sicurezza) is needed.

1vnevbv.q: The speed at which you are travelling affects the safe following distance.
1vnevbv.why: The faster you go, the more metres you cover during reaction time and braking, so more distance is needed.

t2lebr.q: The load carried by the vehicle affects the safe following distance.
t2lebr.why: A heavier or poorly distributed load lengthens braking, so a greater safe following distance is needed.

gmilf1.q: Grip and tyre condition affect the safe following distance.
gmilf1.why: Grip and tyre condition determine the braking distance, on which the safe following distance depends.

1el30k4.q: The number of lanes on the road affects the safe following distance.
1el30k4.why: The number of lanes does not change the vehicle's stopping distance, so it does not affect the safe following distance.

13g9niw.q: The size of the vehicle ahead affects the safe following distance.
13g9niw.why: The distance depends on your own stopping distance, not on the size of the vehicle ahead.

1egpr3j.q: The number of gears in the gearbox affects the safe following distance.
1egpr3j.why: The number of gears does not affect the stopping distance, so it does not affect the safe following distance.

vec1b1.q: The number of wheels of the vehicle affects the safe following distance.
vec1b1.why: The number of wheels is not a factor in determining the safe following distance.

1e2je3n.q: The type of power steering used affects the safe following distance from the vehicle ahead.
1e2je3n.why: The type of power steering does not affect the stopping distance, so it does not affect the safe following distance.

vpud6a.q: The safe following distance does not depend on the type of engine fuel (petrol, diesel, LPG).
vpud6a.why: The fuel type does not change the stopping distance, so the safe following distance does not depend on it.

42jofd.q: The safe following distance depends on the driver's state of health.
42jofd.why: Illness or tiredness lengthens reaction time, so a greater safe following distance (distanza di sicurezza) is needed.

uivc4y.q: The safe following distance depends on the driver's attention and concentration while driving.
uivc4y.why: Less attention means slower reactions, so a greater safe following distance is needed.

cwm912.q: When driving in a queue, it is advisable to increase the safe following distance to avoid chain collisions.
cwm912.why: In a queue, a larger gap gives more time to brake and reduces the risk of chain-reaction rear-end collisions (tamponamenti a catena).

1xw90r4.q: The safe following distance depends on the power of the vehicle ahead.
1xw90r4.why: What matters is your own vehicle's stopping distance, not the power of the vehicle ahead.

1fl5v6k.q: The safe following distance depends on the efficiency of the handbrake.
1fl5v6k.why: The handbrake is not used for braking while driving and does not determine the safe following distance.

wg7rzp.q: The safe following distance depends on the presence of vehicles behind.
wg7rzp.why: The distance depends on your own stopping distance relative to the vehicle ahead, not on vehicles behind.

1ch2gqg.q: The safe following distance must be kept only by motor quadricycles.
1ch2gqg.why: Every driver must keep a safe following distance, whatever the vehicle.

8vodl3.q: The safe following distance must always be kept, even before starting an overtaking manoeuvre.
8vodl3.why: The safe following distance must be kept at all times, including before starting to overtake (sorpasso).

83accw.q: The safe following distance must be increased if it is difficult to judge the behaviour of the driver ahead.
83accw.why: If the driver ahead is unpredictable, more margin is needed to react to sudden manoeuvres.

1h9egwy.q: The safe following distance must be such that the vehicle can be stopped in time in case of danger.
1h9egwy.why: The purpose of the safe following distance is to be able to stop in time and avoid a rear-end collision.

1wxx94w.q: The safe following distance must be at least equal to the metres the vehicle covers during the reaction time.
1wxx94w.why: As a minimum, the gap must equal the distance covered during reaction time, though in practice it should be larger.

1qqmnun.q: The safe following distance must always be equal to the vehicle's braking distance.
1qqmnun.why: The gap must also account for reaction time and conditions; the braking distance alone is not enough.

1gxzdu1.q: The safe following distance must be increased when the vehicle ahead is carrying a protruding, unstable load.
1gxzdu1.why: A protruding, unstable load may fall or cause sudden braking, so more distance is needed.

gea7os.q: The safe following distance must be at least 100 metres in heavy rain.
gea7os.why: There is no fixed 100-metre distance for heavy rain; the gap must simply be increased according to conditions.

1ix0uuh.q: The safe following distance can be reduced in tunnels.
1ix0uuh.why: In tunnels (gallerie) the safe following distance must not be reduced; it should be kept or increased because of limited visibility and risk.

fw2zsl.q: When driving on a motorway, you may reduce the safe following distance, since a sudden braking from the vehicle ahead is not expected.
fw2zsl.why: On the motorway speeds are high and sudden braking is always possible, so the gap must not be reduced.

124ga7z.q: If the vehicle ahead is a lorry, the safe following distance must be reduced, since heavy vehicles have a much longer braking distance than other vehicles.
124ga7z.why: Behind a lorry (autocarro) the gap must not be reduced; what counts is your own stopping distance, and the reduced view ahead calls for caution.
